header.title: The Strategic Position of Atelier Verdant

body_sections.heading: Opening
body_sections.prose: Atelier Verdant occupies a quiet, bespoke quadrant of a market that is loud, mass, and overstimulated. The strategic position is built on patience: refusing the channels that scale fastest in exchange for the channels that hold value longest.

body_sections.heading: The Field
body_sections.prose: Most competitors cluster in either the high-volume / low-bespoke quadrant or the polished, gallery-style high-bespoke quadrant. Atelier Verdant chooses the bespoke axis without the gallery polish: hand-marked, lived-in, plain.

body_sections.heading: The Paradox
body_sections.prose: The brand must grow without scaling. Growth means more pieces, more makers, more rooms. Scaling means standardization, lookbooks, and predictable feeds. The brand commits to the first and refuses the second.

body_sections.heading: Always / Never
body_sections.prose: Strategic commitments are stored as a binding always / never list. The data block below carries them.

body_sections.heading: Three Strategic Priorities
body_sections.prose: Three priorities are ranked. They define what the next quarter is for, and what it is not for.

always: Name the maker on every piece.
Honor every repair request, paid or unpaid.
never: Sell through marketplaces that hide the maker.

items.label: Build the workshop video library.
items.rationale: Provenance is the moat. Without footage of work in progress, the rest of the strategy is rhetorical.

items.label: Open one private viewing per quarter.
items.rationale: The right room with the right audience converts at multiples of the website.

items.label: Refuse two marketplace approaches per quarter.
items.rationale: Discipline is shown by what is declined, not what is signed.
